codeReview.summary: Implementation covers the requested process-management surface overall, but there is one blocking reliability defect in service startup error handling plus two non-blocking contract/edge-case gaps.

issues.description: start_service() starts the subprocess before writing the PID file and does not handle write_pid_file() failure. If PID file write fails (e.g., permission/disk issues), the function raises while leaving the child process running and unmanaged (no PID tracking/cleanup).

start_service() documents raising PortConflictError when a port is already in use, but the function does not call detect_port_conflict()/check_port_conflict(). This creates an API contract mismatch and shifts all safety to callers.
check_port_conflict() ignores LISTEN sockets where psutil reports pid=None and can return None as if the port were free. Under limited process visibility, this can miss real port conflicts.

summary: Review status: fail. The feature is broadly implemented, but startup can leak unmanaged subprocesses when PID-file creation fails; additional non-blocking API/port-detection gaps and a skill-registry mismatch were noted.
